clue.text: Write a note on the expense, a long way to this church

parts.note: to pen is to write
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
expense means cost

explanation.surface: Someone sends a note about how dear and far the journey to a particular church is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way to' is padding linking the pieces to the definition; the church meant is the Pentecostal movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecostal churches form a charismatic Protestant movement stressing gifts of the Holy Spirit.

clue.text: They're laid, for example, on glasses-cases

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: the outside of the word glasses encases it, so its first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: Something is set down, say, on top of spectacle cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens lay them, so things that are laid describes hens' produce.

clue.text: An implement also used by a learner

parts.note: too means also
L is a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A gadget that a trainee happens to use as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is a hand implement for doing work.

clue.text: Flowers eaten by the hundred on this diet

indicators.note: on here means placed first, before the next piece

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the Atkins diet is a well-known low-carbohydrate regime

explanation.surface: Blooms consumed by the hundredweight by someone following a fad diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten by' is a link; the Atkins diet is a low-carbohydrate eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Catkins are the dangling flower spikes of trees such as willow and hazel.

clue.text: Old wine taken by the fire

definitions.meaning: a dry white wine imported from Spain in Shakespeare's day
to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.surface: A vintage drink is carried off by someone near the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sack was a historic fortified white wine; as a verb it means dismiss from employment.

clue.text: Refrain from giving seaman a bad mark

parts.note: AB is able seaman
a stain is a blemish or bad mark

explanation.surface: Advice not to give a sailor a poor grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back from doing something, as voters do when declining to vote.

clue.text: In addition, first of all leave subtraction out!

indicators.note: first of tells us to take the opening letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: An arithmetic instruction: when adding, ignore any taking away.
explanation.definitionFit: Also is a synonym for as well, besides.

clue.text: Toy girl paid wildly for — such extravagance!

indicators.note: wildly tells us to throw these letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl's toy was bought at a ridiculous price, an exclamation at the waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigality is reckless wastefulness with money, as of the prodigal son.

clue.text: Disparagement of those who cannot finish a drink quietly?

indicators.note: cannot finish says the drinking word is cut off before its end

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Contempt for drinkers who can't manage a silent sip.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is noisy, so dropping the quiet P leaves the slur; surface also hints at slurred speech of drunks.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insulting remark that disparages someone.

clue.text: Scepticism shown by eccentric stoic gains 1,000 in support

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: An odd Stoic philosopher wins a thousand backers for his doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' and 'in support' are links: the thousand is added after the jumbled STOIC GAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnosticism is doubt about whether God's existence can be known.

clue.text: Cross via the back entrance

indicators.note: via the back means the entrance word is read from its end

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone crosses over using the rear door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb but is the noun: a rood is a crucifix. 'via the' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Rood is an old word for the crucifix, as in a church's rood screen.

clue.text: Ate in dapper-fashion, that could have been relevant

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone eats like a dandy, which might have mattered.
explanation.definitionFit: To appertain is to pertain or relate to something, so it means being pertinent.

clue.text: An outbreak of germs one may even bless

definitions.text: An outbreak of germs one may even bless

parts.words: An outbreak of germs one may even bless
parts.note: an explosive spray of germs, after which people say 'bless you'

explanation.surface: A spread of infection that someone might nonetheless bless.
explanation.definitionFit: People traditionally say 'bless you' after this germ-spreading expulsion of air.

clue.text: Hang the worker for taking a necklace

parts.note: to pend is to hang, remain undecided
a worker ant

explanation.surface: Execute the labourer for stealing jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is a hanging ornament worn round the neck on a chain.

clue.text: Strained at present, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the present is a grammatical time-form, like past or future

explanation.surface: Things are fraught right now, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense means taut or stressed; in grammar a tense is the verb form marking time, such as present.

clue.text: GIs back-to-back in the navy, with good equipment

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the navy letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: back-to-back means two soldiers stand facing away, so the first is turned around

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
the second of the two GIs

explanation.surface: Two American soldiers stand back-to-back among naval personnel with decent kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigging is the gear of ropes and tackle on a ship; generally, equipment.

clue.text: A sap when it comes to wrongdoing

parts.note: re means regarding, on the subject of
sin is wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone foolish where misbehaviour is concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sap' looks like a fool, but here it is plant fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky sap exuded by trees such as pine.

clue.text: Stick on naughty boy's booze

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
ale is beer, booze

explanation.surface: Stick a label on a bad lad's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce or skewer something on a point.

clue.text: An odd number, unless you deduct the first six

definitions.text: An odd number, unless you deduct the first six

parts.words: An odd number, unless you deduct the first six
parts.note: a number that is odd, but losing the initial letter of six from its name leaves a word meaning not odd

explanation.surface: An odd number stays odd unless you take six away.
explanation.walkthrough: The arithmetic reading misleads: 'the first six' is the letter S, and removing it from the word leaves EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is an odd whole number, between six and eight.

clue.text: An old garden in Wiltshire, densely overgrown

indicators.note: overgrown suggests the garden is covered over by the words around it

explanation.surface: An ancient garden in a southern English county, now thick with weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Wiltshire is a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical garden of Adam and Eve, ancient indeed.

clue.text: Love the friend who gives a jewel!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Treasure the friend who gives you a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone.

clue.text: When the illustration shows jelly…

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as he left'
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: The picture shows a jelly, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury gelatine in which food is set.

clue.text: Rum, perhaps, to keep the coalhole so untidy and unclosed

indicators.note: untidy means messed up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
unclosed says the word loses its closing letter

explanation.surface: Someone stores rum in a messy coal store left open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unclosed' drops the last letter of COALHOLE, leaving COALHOL, which 'untidy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is one example of an alcoholic spirit.

clue.text: Satisfied to list firm number in book

parts.note: Co is company, a firm

indicators.note: in places the number inside the book letters

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Happy to record a company figure in a ledger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to list' is a link here. TEN goes inside NT to give NTENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Content means happy and at ease, wanting nothing more.

clue.text: …it should wobble three times as much, with added mass

indicators.note: with added says the mass letter is put into the threefold word

parts.note: treble means threefold
m is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Following on, something should shake three times harder when heavier.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble is to shake or quiver.

clue.text: Jot down the rent on a card

indicators.note: on means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: to note is to jot down
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: Write down the rent owed on a card.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for brief messages.

clue.text: Abel's murderer may be a member of this tribe

indicators.note: may be hints the name could be reshaped into another word

parts.note: in Genesis Cain killed his brother Abel

explanation.surface: The killer of Abel might belong to this people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were a South American people whose empire centred on Peru.

clue.text: Shear at a smart pace

definitions.meaning: 'at a good ...' means at a brisk speed

explanation.surface: Cut quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip means cut short with shears, and as a noun a brisk speed.

clue.text: A bit of a problem for a small horse

parts.note: S is small
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A minor worry for a pony.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a minor hitch or difficulty.

clue.text: Look over a third of the Nordic countries

indicators.note: a third of means only the opening portion of the region's name is kept

parts.note: Scandinavia covers Norway, Sweden and Denmark

explanation.surface: Survey a third of Northern Europe's nations.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to examine or look through quickly.

clue.text: Welcome bad weather?

definitions.meaning: frozen pellets falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Greeting a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail means to greet or salute, and also icy pellets falling as precipitation.

clue.text: Impromptu lunch — parted at first sign of rain?

indicators.note: impromptu means improvised, so the letters are put together freshly

explanation.surface: An unplanned lunch party breaks up when the first drops fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link. A crash of thunder often heralds a storm, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud crash of thunder often precedes a downpour in a storm.

clue.text: Idle perhaps, or heading for Morecambe

definitions.meaning: ... Idle is a Monty Python comedian
... Morecambe, the British comic of Morecambe and Wise, had this first name

explanation.surface: A lazy person, or someone heading to a seaside town in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is also a Lancashire seaside town, which the surface uses; 'heading' means the first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both comedians, Idle and Morecambe, share the given name.

clue.text: Insulting and devious, to grab lamps so

indicators.note: to grab means the crafty word holds the lamps word inside it

parts.note: sly means devious
lighting covers lamps collectively

explanation.surface: Someone sneaky makes off with lamps in an offensive way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' signals the adverb: insulting in manner. 'to grab' puts LIGHTING between S and LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Slighting means disparaging, so the adverb means in a disrespectful manner.
